feedback:
The machine is faithful, sound, and in the exact required format; accept with two minor notes.

Fidelity. The card has two obligations and both are encoded. (1) Per-client pipeline: u0 waits idle; a client arrival with empty hands enters u1 (order stage), with food in hand enters u2 directly; the order event (+0.1), the pantry pickup (+0.2), preparation (+0.3, u3) and the serve (+1.0, back to accepting u0) reproduce the required order-fetch-prepare-serve chain, and the cycle repeats for each new client. Skipping the order is impossible in the environment (stove and serve both require it), so not tracking order state persistently is sound. (2) Fall recovery: falls in u0 route to r0, where any next step without holding_food sinks to uF (-0.2); falls in u2/u3 self-loop and the following empty-handed, non-fall step sinks to uF; since a slip always lands the food adjacent and facing the agent, the pickup is always feasible on the next move, so the uF trigger never demands the impossible. The strict reading (even taking the order or toggling the switch instead of picking up counts as failure) matches 'your very next move must pick it up'. Siren propositions are correctly ignored as irrelevant and absorbed by per-state else self-loops.

Soundness. Guards in every state partition the label space with mutually exclusive triggers plus an else self-loop; holding_food is used as a persistent condition and the five events as one-step triggers, matching the semantics (e.g. the u2 fall self-loop correctly fires after the order step because order_taken is no longer true). All nine reward entries match existing transitions; unrewarded transitions default to 0. Rewards are dense along the pipeline (0.1/0.2/0.3/1.0, at most 1.6 per client, so bounded), penalties are small and non-farmable (order, prepare, serve each fire at most once per client; no reward is attached to fall pickups, which blocks drop/re-pickup farming). The traced example episode passes without ever touching uF and earns 1.6 for the client, and both order-first and fetch-first orderings yield the same total, so no ordering exploit exists.

Format. Headers REWARD_MACHINE/STATES/INITIAL_STATE/FINAL_STATES/TRANSITION_FUNCTION/REWARD_FUNCTION are present and correctly shaped; FINAL_STATES is nonempty, u0 is declared and is the accepting cycle-complete state reached after every serve; only environment propositions appear in guards.

Minor notes (not grounds for rejection): (a) one exotic corner is unenforced - if the agent drops pre-fetched food in u0, a client arrives, and the agent then picks up exactly on the pending slip's due step, the same-step fall falls into u1's else self-loop, so that particular next-move pickup is not policed; it requires an agent-induced drop plus exact timing and the main flows all enforce the rule. (b) Entry into u2 via client_arrived with a simultaneous fall earns 0 where the holding-food entry earns 0.2, a small uncontrollable asymmetry with no exploitation route.

def holding_food(env): return env.carrying is not None and env.carrying.type == "box"

def switch_toggled(env): return "toggle" in env.events_this_step

def client_arrived(env): return "arrive" in env.events_this_step

def order_taken(env): return "order" in env.events_this_step

def food_prepared(env): return "prepare" in env.events_this_step

def order_served(env): return "serve" in env.events_this_step

def food_fell(env): return "fall" in env.events_this_step

def served_while_ringing(env): return "serve_ringing" in env.events_this_step
